newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Strike talks resume at Brazil's Paranagua port.
newsitem.headline: Strike talks resume at Brazil's Paranagua port.

text.p: Operators and striking dock workers at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua resumed talks on Friday morning after negotiating into the early hours, the port authority said.
"They resumed their meeting at 0900 local/1200 GMT," said a spokeswoman. "They kept going until the early hours."

Port workers at Paranagua have been on strike since midday Wednesday in support of the dock workers' demand for a 21 percent wage increase. The strike is scheduled to continue until midday Saturday unless an early deal is struck.
Officials at the port operators' and dock workers' unions were unavailable for comment early Friday.
The location of their meeting was unclear.

The secretary of the dock workers' union on Thursday ruled out an extension of the strike but said negotiations with the port operators would be drawn out. "We need another 15 to 20 days to agree on all the points, it's not that easy," he said.
The port operators' union SINDOP said the strike was costing the port $3 million per day. The port authority declined to put a value on the cost of the strike.
